answer.sourceLine: Widely credited to Musk, and in his style, but no interview, speech, post or transcript has been found with these words. The oldest print appearance this check found is Shane Snow’s 2014 book Smartcuts, which calls it something “Musk likes to say” and gives no source.

source.excerptNote: Shane Snow’s wording in Smartcuts (2014), read through the Internet Archive’s full-text search. Snow presents the line as a habitual saying of Musk’s. He does not name an interview, speech or date.
source.rightsNote: No speech, interview, post or book by Musk containing this wording has been identified, so no rights status can be assigned to it. The oldest print appearance found, Shane Snow’s Smartcuts (HarperBusiness, 2014), is a modern in-copyright book, but Snow is reporting the line as Musk’s saying, not claiming to have written it.

misattribution.heading: Why the credit is shaky
misattribution.intro: The line is everywhere under Musk’s name: quote sites, listicles, yearbooks, social media. Every copy traced here leads back to another secondary source, never to Musk himself.

items.why: Goodreads credits Musk with no source and notes that its quotes are user-added and unverified. It also drops the semicolon (“possible then probability”), one of several wording drifts. Goodreads ↗
Not on Musk’s main Wikiquote page, which collects sourced quotes year by year. It sits on the talk page under “Further unsourced quotes,” backed only by an Inc. listicle. Talk:Elon Musk ↗

items.who: Elon Musk (as reported by Shane Snow)
items.why: Smartcuts (2014) frames it as a habitual saying, “as Musk likes to say,” without naming when or where he said it. Internet Archive ↗

misattribution.truthLine: No Musk interview, talk, post or transcript containing these words has been produced. The oldest appearance found is a 2014 book that reports it secondhand, so treat it as attributed, not verified. Wikiquote’s unsourced list ↗

context.heading: How the line spread
lead: In Smartcuts, journalist Shane Snow uses the line in his discussion of what he calls “10x thinking,” alongside his account of Musk building a space company. Snow’s notes say he sent the chapter to Musk for firsthand verification and that Musk did not return anything. So the book gives no confirmation from Musk of this wording.

From there the sentence moved into quote databases and motivational lists, then into school yearbooks and social posts. Each copy cites the one before it or nothing at all. It may well be something Musk has said, but nobody has yet pointed to the recording or text where he said it.
